title.value: CMIMP: Effortlessly Achieving Diverse Population Training for Zero-Shot Coordination

abstract.value: Zero-shot coordination has recently become a hot topic in reinforcement learning research recently. It focuses on the generalization ability of agents, requiring them to coordinate well with collaborators that are not seen before without any fine-tuning. Population-based training has been proven to provide good zero-shot coordination performance; nevertheless, existing algorithms exhibit inefficiency, as the training cost scales linearly with the population size. To address this issue, this paper proposes the  Conditional Mutual Information Maximized Population (CMIMP), an efficient training framework comprising two key components: a meta-agent that efficiently realizes a population by selectively sharing parameters across agents, and a mutual information regularizer that guarantees population diversity. To empirically validate the effectiveness of CMIMP, this paper evaluates it along with representational frameworks in Hanabi and confirms its superiority.
